# Results

**Scope:** adidas AG, one backtest point (built as of FY2024, checked against FY2025 actuals). Generated by `src/report.py` — regenerate with `make report` after any model change.

## Bottom line

The driver-based forecast beat a naive top-down extrapolation on every backtested metric, but both undershot actual FY2025 operating profit (€2,056m) — adidas guided €1.7–1.8bn and delivered more. "The driver-based model won" is not the same claim as "the driver-based model was accurate."

| metric | naive error | driver-based error | actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 5.5% | 3.1% | €24,811m |
| Operating profit | 22.3% | 14.9% | €2,056m |
| Free cash flow | 14.8% | 3.4% | €1,106m |

## Monte Carlo: which assumption actually drives the uncertainty

![Monte Carlo free cash flow distribution](data/monte_carlo_fcf.png)

10,000 draws sampled from adidas's own disclosed FY2025 guidance ranges — not invented historical volatility; three fiscal years is too few to estimate that honestly (see `src/scenario.py`).

| | |
|---|---|
| Downside (P10) | €963m |
| Median (P50) | €1,070m |
| Upside (P90) | €1,178m |
| Actual FY2025 (derived) | €1,106m |

Sensitivity of simulated free cash flow to each assumption, ranked by absolute correlation:

| assumption | correlation with FCF |
|---|---|
| working capital | -0.92 |
| operating profit target | +0.27 |
| capex | -0.22 |
| revenue growth | -0.19 |

**Working capital dominates** — a wider or narrower revenue-growth assumption barely moves the free-cash-flow outcome by comparison. The naive method's biggest miss was exactly this: it held working capital flat at FY2024's level while it actually rose. Review time is better spent stress-testing the working-capital assumption than re-arguing the growth rate.

## What this is not

- **A track record.** One backtest point. A single win is evidence the driver-based approach beat one naive baseline once, not that it generalizes.
- **Statistically estimated uncertainty.** The Monte Carlo ranges are adidas's own disclosed guidance bands, chosen because three fiscal years cannot support a real volatility estimate.
